chapter_theme: A song at Thiruppoonthuruthi (திருப்பூந்துருத்தி): after a frank picture of lovemaking, the poet asks that the cravings of food, union and maya end and that he be given the conduct of true knowledge; the praise is a run of epithets for Murugan as commander, teacher and healer of devotees.

888.reading: The poet describes the embrace, breasts like tender coconuts, lips sweet as sugar, milk and honey, garments parted, eyes striking the earrings, love-cries and Kama's many kinds of play, and asks that, with the cravings of food, union and maya ended, Murugan give him the conduct of true knowledge that makes him easy to reach. The praise calls Murugan commander of the gods' army, Rudra's son, rider of the peacock, praised by sages and Indra, the calm wise teacher wearing the kadamba garland, lord of Seyppathi, the hero with a mountain-like form, who grants grace so that his devotees' diseases leave them, at Poonthuruthi.
888.nuance: ஊண் புணர்ச்சியுமாயா வாதனை: hunger, union and maya are named together as the vasanas (traces) to end. மெய்ஞ்ஞான ஆசாரம்: knowledge is asked as a conduct, not only a vision. போந்த பத்தர் பொலா நோய் போயிட: Murugan as healer. Several epithets in the praise are corrupt or obscure (சாங்கிபர், சீநாதீசுரர், ¡£பகிரண்ட்ருபா).

links.note: 888 asks that the cravings of food, union and maya end (ஊண் புணர்ச்சியுமாயா வாதனை தீர்ந்து) and that Murugan give the conduct of true knowledge (மெய்ஞ்ஞான ஆசாரம்). Tirumanthiram 556 sets out such a conduct: purity, compassion, little food (ஊண் சுருக்கம்), forbearance, truth, and seeing lust for what it is (காமம் ... எனக் காண்பவை). The song names the conduct in a phrase as a gift; the Tirumanthiram spells it out as rules, beginning with the same two cravings, food and lust.
